chunks: Whoever intends evil against the Kaaba.

No one intended evil against the Kaaba except that Allah, Mighty and Majestic, became angry for its sake. One day, King Tubba' resolved to kill the fighting men of the people of the Kaaba, enslave their offspring, and then demolish the Kaaba. His eyes flowed until they fell upon his cheeks. He asked about that, and they said: We see that what has afflicted you is only because of what you intended regarding this House, for the land is the sanctuary of Allah, the House is the House of Allah, and the inhabitants of Mecca are the descendants of Ibrahim, the close friend of Allah. He said: You have spoken the truth; so what is my way out of what I have fallen into? They said: Turn your mind to something other than that. So he turned his mind toward good, and his pupils returned until they were fixed in their place. Then he summoned the people who had advised him to demolish it and killed them. Then he came to the House and clothed it with leather coverings, and fed food for thirty days, one hundred camels each day, until large bowls were carried to the beasts on the mountaintops and fodder was scattered for the wild animals. Then he departed from Mecca to Medina and settled there a people from the people of Yemen, from Ghassan, and they are the Ansar.

And it has been narrated that he slaughtered for it six thousand cattle at Shi'b Ibn 'Amir, and it used to be called the kitchens of Tubba' until Ibn 'Amir settled there, so it was ascribed to him and it was said: Shi'b Ibn 'Amir. Tubba' was neither a believer nor a disbeliever, but he was among those who sought the upright religion. None ruled the East except Tubba' and Kisra.
And the companions of the elephant, and their king Abu Yaksum, Abraha ibn al-Sabah al-Himyari, set out toward it to demolish it.
So Allah sent against them flocks of birds, pelting them with stones of baked clay, and He made them like eaten straw.

What befell Tubba' and the companions of the elephant did not befall al-Hajjaj because al-Hajjaj's aim was not the demolition of the Kaaba; rather, his aim was Ibn al-Zubayr, and he was opposed to the possessor of the truth. So when he sought refuge in the Kaaba, Allah willed to make clear to the people that He had not granted him refuge, and so He gave respite to the one who demolished it against him.

key_terms.أَصْحَابُ الْفِيلِ: the people of the elephant who came to attack the Kaaba
key_terms.الْأَنْصَارُ: the helpers, identified here as a group settled in Medina
key_terms.حَرَمُ اللَّهِ: the sacred sanctuary established by Allah
key_terms.سِجِّيلٍ: baked clay or hard stones sent as punishment
key_terms.طَيْرًا أَبَابِيلَ: flocks of birds sent by Allah against the attackers

ai.seo_question: What happens to those who intend evil against the Kaaba in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This report describes the sanctity of the Kaaba and how intending harm against it brings divine anger. It recounts historical examples of those who sought to attack it and explains that divine response differed according to intention and circumstance.
